references.text: Moses hides his face because he is afraid to see God, which underscores the fear of meeting the living God face to face.
God says that no one can see His face and live, confirming the idea that it is extraordinary to hear the voice of the living God and survive.
The question is raised whether any people have heard the voice of God speaking from the fire and remained alive, a parallel to this verse.
Joshua refers to the living God who is in the midst of the people, using the same expression 'living God'.
David uses the phrase 'armies of the living God' when he confronts Goliath, referring to the God of Israel as the living God.
Isaiah fears for his life because he has seen the Lord, the King, and is a man with unclean lips.
It is terrible to fall into the hands of the living God, which underscores the awe due to the living God.
Our God is a consuming fire, connecting to the image of God speaking from the fire.
